candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Case Management/Continuity of Care/Performance Improvement: coordinate multidisciplinary care, evaluate care-delivery approaches and outcomes, support discharge/follow-up, and facilitate continuity across settings.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — outcomes of coordinated multidisciplinary heart-failure disease management
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that coordinated multidisciplinary heart-failure disease-management and self-care programs can improve important outcomes, including reduced heart-failure hospitalization and improved quality of life, without replacing ongoing clinical care.

options.A: Such coordinated multidisciplinary and self-care interventions can reduce heart-failure-related hospitalization and may improve quality of life and other clinical outcomes.
options.B: These programs have no demonstrated relationship to hospitalization or self-care outcomes and are used mainly for administrative scheduling.
options.C: The programs are beneficial only when they replace the client's usual clinicians and become the sole source of ongoing heart-failure care.
options.D: The programs are appropriate only for clients awaiting transplant and are not relevant to broader chronic heart-failure management.

candidate.rationale: The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline summarizes meta-analyses showing that multidisciplinary interventions can reduce heart-failure and all-cause hospitalizations and that structured self-care interventions can reduce heart-failure hospitalization and improve quality of life. Programs that include medication-adherence support and coordinated case management are part of this evidence base. Therefore, A accurately reflects the guideline. B denies documented benefits, C incorrectly substitutes the program for longitudinal clinicians, and D restricts these interventions to a population not specified by the evidence.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports coordinated multidisciplinary/case-management and self-care interventions as strategies associated with reduced hospitalization and improved quality of life in heart failure.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: Multidisciplinary/self-care supportive text preceding Section 7.3: meta-analysis of 30 RCTs found multidisciplinary interventions reduced hospital admission and all-cause mortality; meta-analysis of 22 RCTs found specialized multidisciplinary follow-up associated with reduced HF/all-cause hospitalization; case-management and multidisciplinary interventions reduced readmission; self-care interventions reduced HF-related hospitalization and improved quality of life; medication-adherence and structured support interventions were effective. Section 9.6 also supports coordinated team-based transition systems.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.stem: A health system is evaluating a multidisciplinary heart-failure disease-management program that combines coordinated follow-up, self-care education, and medication-adherence support. Which outcome is most consistent with the AHA/ACC/HFSA evidence summary?
